synthesis.description: A logistics lead or manager announces who now handles which pooling points, industrial accounts, counterparties or duties, usually when someone joins, leaves or a desk is realigned. Recipients reply to confirm or to point out pieces that look unassigned, and departing or moving staff confirm what they hand over. Some rounds introduce new staff or share contact extensions so others know whom to call for work moved off another desk.
steps: A staff change, reorganisation or new account triggers a reassignment.
The lead drafts a memo listing each pipeline, point or account and its new owner and backup.
The memo is sent to the desk and forwarded to affected groups.
Recipients check the list against what they handle and flag gaps or items left unassigned.
Outgoing and incoming owners confirm the handover of specific accounts.
A follow-up memo settles the open items and contact details.
synthesis.approach: Keep one shared assignment register listing every pipeline, pooling point, account and duty with its owner and backup. A reassignment memo is generated from the changes to the register, and any item without an owner is flagged before the memo goes out.
synthesis.rationale: The confusion in the mail comes from items missing from free-text memos. A register laid out by item, owner and backup makes gaps visible and gives the desk one place to check who handles what.
